attempts.raw_response: GOSCHEN, who having spent a lifetime inquiring which way the wind blows, now finds himself becalmed in the doldrums between the Treasury bench and the Opposition. He gazes wistfully across the floor, a political amphibian uncertain whether to swim with the tide of office or crawl back to the barren rocks of independence. Mr. RITCHSON, too, lingers in the corridor of indecision, his allegiance as flexible as a parliamentary whip's conscience. These are the men who wait upon events, who calculate and recalculate, hoping somehow to emerge upon the winning side without ever having committed themselves to the hazard. Meanwhile, the gallant General must marshal such forces as he can, corner-seat or no, and trust that the country will forgive a leader who hesitates when he should charge.

be in permanent session in order that the world might have the daily

the MINISTER OF RECONSTRUCTION, to whom the missing Question was
addressed, that, when asked where his department was located, he
had to confess that he did not know the precise number, but it was
somewhere in Queen Anne's Gate.
